newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - June 3.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - June 3.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Tuesday:
** Indian manufacturing industry is expected pick up in the coming months, governor of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) said on Monday.
"I expect manufacturing (sector) to pick up in the coming months," RBI governor Chakravarty Rangarajan told businessmen and economists at the Indian Merchants Chamber.

Several sectors of the manufacturing sector showed a slowdown in 1996/97 (April-March). Rangarajan said credit availability rose in recent months, the rate of interest was comfortable, and there was an impending revival in the manufacturing sector.

** Foreign institutional investors have increased their holding in Bharat Heavy Electricals Ltd (BHEL) and currently have a total stake of 16 percent, up by about four percent over the last one year, the Economic Times reports.

** In one of the first cases where pension funds have invested in Indian infrastructure companies, Nynex Corporation Master Pension Trust and GT Service Corporation Pension Plan of the US have picked up stakes in BHEL, the paper says.
** Mercedes-Benz India Ltd on Monday said its German parent Daimler-Benz AG plans to raise its share capital in the Indian firm assembling Mercedes luxury cars.

It said Tata Engineering and Locomotive Company Ltd (TELCO), its Indian partner owning 49 percent of Mercedes-Benz India, welcomed the firm's plan to raise exports and boost local Indian component suppliers.

"This programme may necessitate a further infusion of funds. In view of TELCO's investment commitments to its own business growth, it has been agreed between the partners that TELCO would not participate in the current capital increase," it said.
** The Indian rupee opened unchanged at 35.8050/8150 against the dollar on Tuesday, dealers said. The day's range is seen at 35.78/81 rupees to a dollar, they said.
** Indian blue chips sprang higher on Monday led by a nearly 10 percent jump in index-linked stock ITC, traders said.
** Bombay's benchmark stocks index ended 53.08 points, or 1.41 percent, up at 3,808.18.
